captions.text: Our basis vectors span one square.
Nearby sits a leaf, filled with tiny squares.
This matrix stretches two wide, three tall.
Every one becomes a two by three rectangle: six times bigger.
So the whole leaf grows sixfold.
What about a bigger leaf, far away? Any guess?
Times six again. Size and position don't matter.
Because every region is made of those same squares.
Let's undo that, and try a less tidy map.
This matrix has columns two, one and one, two.
Our basis vectors land on them; the square slants.
Now pick any grid cell and slide it over.
A perfect fit. Try another one.
Every cell is that same parallelogram, wherever it started.
So square and leaf should grow by one factor.
That factor, the parallelogram's area, is the determinant of A.
Here it's three: one number for the whole plane.
